items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: Then there was Piku, Teo, all those guys, man.

ctx.x: Yes. When you got to New Orleans, who was the best down at play in town next to you?

Well, no, that's kind of a whole dance. That's a loaded question. Yeah, because I still like Joe Watson to my idea. Then there was Zell, he was with Redhead, yeah, he was with Redhead, he was supposed to beat him. Oh, yeah. Then there was Piku, Teo, all those guys, man.
Did Piku play much jazz in those days?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: And then I had this fellow, T.O. used to play a lot of clarinet, too, with P. Ron. But he was mostly a reading man

ctx.x: He maybe do, but I haven't seen him play in a long time. Matter of fact, I haven't heard him play anything in a long time. I run across him every night, and then, yeah, he passes by my house. Mm-hmm. And then I had this fellow, T.O. used to play a lot of clarinet, too, with P. Ron. But he was mostly a reading man, to sit out and play that music.
Well, how did he do if he got in some Barrel House place and had to cut loose? Suppose he...
